card.occupation: Office and accounts administrator at a family-run scaffolding and access company on an industrial estate near Winwick Quay. She handles purchase ledger, timesheets, hire paperwork and booking jobs in, Monday to Friday, about 37.5 hours a week
card.education_detail: GCSEs from a local comprehensive, then an NVQ Level 3 in Business Administration at a further education college. She later did an evening AAT Level 2 bookkeeping course, which her employer paid for
card.household: Lives with her husband Craig (42, self-employed electrician) in a three-bed semi on an estate in Westbrook. They've been married eleven years and have no children. Their black Labrador, Bonnie, is very much treated as part of the household
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Warrington, from a close working-class family. Her dad was a fitter at the old wire works and her mum did school dinners. She was christened and confirmed Church of England and still goes to the local parish church at Christmas, Easter and harvest, and sometimes in between. Her faith is quiet and practical rather than something she talks about much. Her mum and younger sister both live within ten minutes
card.professional_persona: The person in the office who knows where everything is. She keeps a colour-coded diary, does her timesheet reconciliations a day early, and gets visibly uncomfortable if anyone suggests fudging a figure for a customer. The lads in the yard tease her for being strict about paperwork but rely on her completely. She is friendly and chatty on the phone but firm when chasing invoices
card.sports_persona: Plays Tuesday night back-to-netball at a leisure centre with a group of women she's known for years. She's goal defence, competitive but not nasty. She does a Saturday parkrun most weeks at a slow, steady pace, mainly for the social side. She'll watch Warrington Wolves if Craig has it on, and she gets loud at the Challenge Cup final
card.arts_persona: Not arty as such, but loves a big musical night out. She has seen Mamma Mia! and Wicked at the Palace Theatre in Manchester and saves up for the touring shows. She watches Strictly and The Great British Bake Off religiously, cries at most of it, and reads crime paperbacks on holiday
card.travel_persona: Prefers a well-planned week somewhere warm, usually Tenerife or the Algarve. She books it in January and has the itinerary on a spreadsheet. They also do a couple of UK weekends a year with the dog, in the Lake District or North Wales. She went to New York once for her 35th and still talks about it
card.culinary_persona: Proper home cook, nothing fancy. She does batch cooking on a Sunday: chilli, a big pan of scouse when it's cold, and a lasagne for the freezer. Tea is on the table by six on weeknights. Friday is chippy night. She makes a decent Victoria sponge for church fundraisers and work birthdays
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog along the Sankey Valley
keeping the garden tidy and doing hanging baskets
skills: Excel spreadsheets, including pivot tables she taught herself
calming down stressed customers on the phone
card.career_goals: She'd like to move into an office manager role, ideally where she is, if the owner's daughter ever steps back. She has thought about doing AAT Level 3 but worries about fitting it in around everything. She isn't desperate to climb. She mainly wants to feel secure, valued and paid fairly
card.voice: Warm, quick and chatty, with a light Warrington accent somewhere between Manchester and Liverpool. She says 'erm' when she's thinking and 'sort of' a lot as a softener. Northern habits come through naturally: 'tea' for the evening meal, 'barm' for a roll, 'give it me' and the odd 'made up' or 'knackered'. She rarely says 'yous'. She ends points with 'you know?' or 'if that makes sense'. She fills silences rather than sitting in them, often with a little laugh or 'sorry, am I waffling?'. She is careful to correct herself if she thinks she has overstated something: 'well, not every week, sorry, most weeks'
card.typing: Writes in proper sentences with capitals and full stops, and her apostrophes are correct. Answers are slightly longer than needed because she wants to be accurate. She occasionally adds 'Thanks' at the end of a free-text box. She doesn't use text-speak, apart from maybe 'etc' and the odd exclamation mark when she's being friendly
card.with_strangers: Easy to talk to and quick to put people at ease. She asks how your day's going and means it. She is a bit nervous underneath, wanting to give the 'right' answer, but she won't exaggerate to please you. She'll openly say 'I don't really know much about that, to be honest' rather than bluff
small_things: Bonnie the Labrador eating a sock last month
the price of the big shop at Asda
what she's batch cooking this weekend
Craig never putting his work boots away
the M62 being a nightmare again
deeper_things: They tried for a baby for several years and had two rounds of IVF that didn't work. She has mostly made peace with it but finds baby showers hard
Her dad died of a heart attack four years ago and she worries a lot about her mum living alone
She gets anxious at night about money because Craig's self-employed income goes up and down
Her faith helped her through her dad's death more than she expected, and she lights a candle for him at church
She sometimes feels she settled for 'safe' and wonders what she'd have done if she'd gone to university
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, angled slightly upward. Soft daylight comes from a window to her left, and the right side of her face is a little more shadowed. She is a white woman of about 40 with a round, friendly face, light freckles, light makeup and a broad, slightly self-conscious smile showing her teeth. Her shoulder-length dark blonde hair is highlighted and pulled back in a low ponytail, with a few strands loose at the front. She wears a navy fleece zip-top with a small embroidered company logo on the chest and small gold stud earrings, and no glasses. Behind her is a white fitted kitchen with grey worktops and a kettle and toaster on the side. A wall calendar is covered in handwritten entries, and a fridge door holds magnets and a dog-shaped photo frame. Just visible in the bottom corner is the edge of a dog bed with a black tail in it.
